questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The density (in $\mathrm{g} \mathrm{cm}^{-3}$ ) of the metal which forms a cubic close packed (ccp) lattice with an axial distance (edge length) equal to 400 pm is $\qquad$ .
Use: Atomic mass of metal $=105.6 \mathrm{amu}$ and Avogadro's constant $=6 \times 10^{23} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text{ CCP : } \\ & (\mathrm{Z}=4, \mathrm{a}=400 \mathrm{pm}, \mathrm{M}=105.6 \mathrm{ g} / \mathrm{mol}) \\ & \text{ Density }=\frac{\mathrm{Z} \times \mathrm{M}}{\mathrm{a}^3 \times \mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{A}}} \\ & =\frac{4 \times 105.6}{\left(400 \times 10^{-10}\right)^3 \times 6 \times 10^{23}}=11.00 \mathrm{ g} / \mathrm{cm}^3\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
Atoms of metals $x, y$ and $z$ form face-centred cubic (fcc) unit cell of edge length ${L}_{x}$, body-centred cubic (bcc) unit cell of edge length ${L}_{y}$, and simple cubic unit cell of edge length ${L}_{z}$, respectively. If ${r}_{z} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}{r}_{y}; {r}_{y} = \dfrac{8}{\sqrt{3}}{r}_{x}; {M}_{z} = \dfrac{3}{2}{M}_{y}$ and ${M}_{z} = 3{M}_{x}$, then the correct statement(s) is(are)

[Given: ${M}_{x}, {M}_{y}$, and ${M}_{z}$ are molar masses of metals $x, y$, and $z$, respectively. ${r}_{x}, {r}_{y}$, and ${r}_{z}$ are atomic radii of metals $x, y$, and $z$, respectively.]
options: Packing efficiency of unit cell of $x >$ Packing efficiency of unit cell of $y >$ Packing efficiency of unit cell of $z$
questions.solution:
Metal $x$ forms FCC (edge length ${L}_{x}$ )

Metal y forms BCC (edge length ${L}_{y}$ )

Metal $z$ forms SC (edge length ${L}_{z}$ )

Given ${r}_{z} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}{r}_{y}$ and ${r}_{y} = \dfrac{8}{\sqrt{3}}{r}_{x}$

$∴ {r}_{z} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \times \dfrac{8}{\sqrt{3}}{r}_{x} = 4{r}_{x}$

${M}_{z} = \dfrac{3}{2}{M}_{y}{M}_{z} = 3{M}_{x}$

$∴ {M}_{y} = 2{M}_{x}$

Packing efficiency $FCC > BCC > SC$

Packing efficiency unit cell $x > y > z$

In FCC unit cell:- atoms along the face diagonals are in contact.

$∴ \sqrt{2}{L}_{x} = 4{r}_{x} ⇒ {L}_{x} = 2\sqrt{2}{r}_{x}$

In BCC unit cell: atoms along the body diagonal are

$∴ \sqrt{3}{L}_{y} = 4{r}_{y} ⇒ {L}_{y} = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{3}}{r}_{y} = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{3}} \times \dfrac{8}{\sqrt{3}}{r}_{x} = \dfrac{32}{3}{r}_{x}$

${L}_{y} = \dfrac{32}{3}{r}_{x}$

In SC unit cell, atoms along the edge are in contact

$∴ {L}_{z} = 2{r}_{z}$

$= 2 \times 4{r}_{x} = 8{r}_{x}$

${L}_{x} = 2\sqrt{2}{r}_{x}$

${L}_{y} = \dfrac{32}{3}{r}_{x}$

${L}_{z} = 8{r}_{x}$

$∴ {L}_{y} > {L}_{z} > {L}_{x}$

Density of $x$ (Number of atoms of $x$ per unit cell $( z ) = 4 )$

${d}_{x} = \dfrac{{zM}_{x}}{{\left({L}_{x}\right)}^{3}{N}_{A}} = \dfrac{4 \times {M}_{x}}{{\left(2\sqrt{2}{r}_{x}\right)}^{3} \times {N}_{A}}$

$= \dfrac{4{M}_{x}}{16\sqrt{2}{r}_{x}^{3}{N}_{A}} = \dfrac{{M}_{x}}{4\sqrt{2}{r}_{x}^{3}{N}_{A}}$

Density of $y$ : (Number of atoms of y per unit cell $( z ) = 2$ )

${d}_{y} = \dfrac{{zM}_{y}}{{\left({L}_{y}\right)}^{3}{N}_{A}} = \dfrac{2 \times 2{M}_{x}}{{\left(\dfrac{32}{3}{r}_{x}\right)}^{3}{N}_{A}} = \dfrac{108{M}_{x}}{32768{r}_{x}^{3}{N}_{A}}$

$∴$ Density of $x >$ density of $y$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Atom $X$ occupies the fcc lattice sites as well as alternate tetrahedral voids of the same lattice. The packing efficiency (in $%$) of the resultant solid is closest to
questions.solution:
Atom $X$ occupies FCC lattice sites as well as alternate tetrahedral voids of FCC. In FCC, tetrahedral voids are $8$ (in a unit cell) Hence

Atom $X$ in a unit cell (FCC lattice sites)

$= 8 \times \dfrac{1}{8} + 6 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 4$

Atom $X$ in a unit cell (in T.V.) $= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 8 = 4$

Total atom$X$ in one unit cell $= 8$

For relation between a and r, since Tetrahedral void forms at $\dfrac{1}{4}$th of body diagonal,

$\dfrac{a\sqrt{3}}{4} = 2r$

$a = \dfrac{8r}{\sqrt{3}}$

Packing efficiency $= \dfrac{8 \times \dfrac{4}{3}{\pi r}^{3}}{{a}^{3}} \times 100 = \dfrac{8 \times \dfrac{4}{3}{\pi r}^{3}}{{\left(\dfrac{8r}{\sqrt{3}}\right)}^{3}} \times 100 = 35 %$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For the given close packed structure of a salt made of cation $X$ and anion $Y$ shown below (ions of only one face are shown for clarity), the packing fraction is approximately (packing fraction $= \dfrac{packingefficiency}{100}$)
questions.solution:
Total number of atoms in a unit cell

No. of $x$ $= 6 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 3$ atom (at face centres)

No. of $y$ $= 8 \times \dfrac{1}{8} = 1$ atom (at all corners)

So, the formula of compound is ${x}_{3}y$

Now

If radius of $x$ is $r$ and radius of $y$ is $R$ then side length $a = 2R$

and face diagonal $\sqrt{2}a = 2R + 2r$

$r = \left(\sqrt{2} - 1\right)R$

Now Packing fraction $= \dfrac{volumeofatoms}{Volumeofunitcell}$

$= \dfrac{1 \times \dfrac{4}{3}{\pi R}^{3} + 3 \times \dfrac{4}{3}{\pi r}^{3}}{{a}^{3}}$

Substituting $a = 2R$ and $r = 0 . 414R$

$= \dfrac{\dfrac{4}{3}{\pi R}^{3}\left(1 + 3{\left(0 . 414\right)}^{3}\right)}{{\left(2R\right)}^{3}}$

$= \dfrac{4\pi}{3 \times 8}\left(1 + 0 . 07096 \times 3\right)$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{6} \times 1 . 212 = 0 . 63$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider an ionic solid $MX$, with $NaCl$ structure. Construct a new structure $\left(Z\right)$, whose unit cell is constructed from the unit cell of $MX$, following the sequential instructions given below. Neglect the charge balance.
$( i )$ Remove all the anions $\left(X\right)$, except the central one.
$( ii )$ Replace all the face centered cations $\left(M\right)$, by anions $\left(X\right)$.
$( iii )$ Remove all the corner cations $\left(M\right)$.
$( iv )$ Replace the central anion $\left(X\right)$, with cation $\left(M\right)$.
The value of $\left(\dfrac{numberofanions}{numberofcations}\right) in Z$ is _____.
questions.solution:
${X}^{-} ⇒ O . V$
${M}^{+} ⇒ FCC$
${M}^{+}$ $X ^ -$
(i) 4 1
(ii) 4 – 3 3 + 1
(iii) 4 – 3 – 1 3 + 1
(iv) 1 3
$Z = \dfrac{3}{1} = 3$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A crystalline solid of a pure substance has a face-centred cubic structure with a cell edge of $400pm$ . If the density of the substance in the crystal is $8g{cm}^{- 3},$ then the number of atoms present in $256g$ of the crystal $isN \times {10}^{24}$ . The value of $N$is
questions.solution:
Formula of density $= \dfrac{Z \times M}{{N}_{A} \times {a}^{3}}$

For FCC unit cell $Z, = 4$

Edge length, $a = 4 \times {10}^{- 8}cm$

$M = \dfrac{d \times {N}_{A} \times {a}^{3}}{Z} = \dfrac{8 \times 6 \times {10}^{23} \times 64 \times {10}^{- 24}}{4}g / mol$

Number of atoms $= \dfrac{wt\left(g\right)}{molarmass} \times {N}_{A} = \dfrac{256 \times 10 \times 6 \times {10}^{23}}{8 \times 6 \times 16} = 2 \times {10}^{24}$

Hence, the required value of $N = 2$

questions.q: The CORRECT statement(s) for cubic close packed (ccp) three dimensional structure is (are)
options: The number of the nearest neighbours of an atom present in the topmost layer is 12
The efficiency of atom packing is  $74%$
The number of octahedral and tetrahedral voids per atom are 1 and 2, respectively
The unit cell edge length is $2\sqrt{2}$ times the radius of the atom
questions.solution:
CCP is ABC ABC ..... type packing

B] Packing fraction $= \dfrac{4 \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{r}^{3}}{{\left(\dfrac{4r}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}^{3}} = \left(0.74\right)$
C] Each FCC unit has effective no of atoms = 4
Octahedral void = 4
Tetrahedral void = 8
D] $4r = a\sqrt{2}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: If the unit cell of a mineral has cubic close packed (ccp) array of oxygen atoms with m fraction of octahedral holes occupied by aluminium ions and n fraction of tetrahedral holes occupied by magnesium ions, m and n, respectively, are
questions.solution:
In ccp, ${O}^{2 -}$ ions are 4.
Hence total negative charge = -8
Let $A{l}^{3 +}$ ions be x, and $M{g}^{2 +}$ ions be y.
Total positive charge = 3x + 2y
$⇒ 3x + 2y = 8$
This relation is satisfied only by x = 2 and y = 1.
Hence number of $A{l}^{3 +} = 2$
and number of $M{g}^{2 +} = 1$
$⇒$ n = fraction of octahedral holes occupied by $A{l}^{3 +}$
$= \dfrac{2}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}$
and m = fraction of tetrahedral holes occupied by $M{g}^{2 +}$
$= \dfrac{1}{8}$

questions.q: Silver (atomic weight $=108 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ ) has a density of $10.5 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3}$. The number of silver atoms on a surface of area $10^{-12} \mathrm{~m}^2$ can be expressed in scientific notation as $y \times 10^x$. The value of $x$ is
questions.solution:
Volume of one mole of silver atoms =$\frac{108}{10.5} \mathrm{ cm}^3$ /mole Volume of $one silver atom =\frac{108}{10.5} \times \frac{1}{6.022 \times 10^{23}} \mathrm{ cm}^3 
So,
 
\begin{aligned}
\frac{4}{3} \pi R^3 & =\frac{108}{10.5} \times \frac{1}{6.022 \times 10^{23}}=1.708 \times 10^{-23} \\
R^3 & =0.407 \times 10^{-23} \mathrm{ cm}^3 \\
& =0.407 \times 10^{-29} \mathrm{ m}^3
\end{aligned}
 
Area of each silver atom
 
\pi R^2=\pi \times\left(0.407 \times 10^{-29} \mathrm{ m}^3\right)^{2 / 3}
 
So number of silver atoms in given area
 
=\frac{10^{-12}}{\left(0.407 \times 10^{-29} \mathrm{ m}^3\right)^{2 / 3}}=\frac{10^8}{(\pi \times 2)}=1.6 \times 10^7=y \times 10^x \quad \text{ so, } \quad x=7
 
Solid state
Mathematical understanding
III$

Trapping of an electron in the lattice leads to the formation of F-centre

Schottky defects have no effect on the physical properties of solids
questions.solution:
(a) Wrong Frenkel defect is favoured when the difference in ionic radii is very large. In the given case Schottky defect is favoured.
(b) Correct Frenkel defect arises due to dislocation of smaller ion from its normal lattice point to the interstitial space.
(c) Correct When alkali metal in the gaseous state is passed over salts like $\mathrm{NaCl}$, electrons from metal are trapped in the interstitial space giving rise to F-centre defect which is a type of Frenkel defect.
(d) Wrong Schottky defect affects physical properties of solids.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Paragraph: In hexagonal system of crystals, a frequently encountered arrangement of atoms is described as a hexagonal prism. Here, the top and bottom of the cell are regular hexagons and three atoms are sandwiched in between them. A space-filling model of this structure, called hexagonal close-packed (HCP), is constituted of a sphere on a flat surface surrounded in the same plane by six identical spheres as closely as possible. Three spheres are then placed over the first layer so that they touch each other and represent the second layer. Each one of the three spheres touches three spheres of the bottom layer. Finally, the second layer is covered with a third layer that is identical to the bottom layer in relative position. Assume radius of every sphere to be ' $r$ '.Question: The number of atoms in this HCP unit cell is
questions.solution: The effective number of atoms in the hcp is $=12 \times \frac{1}{6}+2 \times \frac{1}{2}+3=6$

Assume radius of every sphere to be ' $r$ '.Question: The volume of this $\mathrm{HCP}$ unit cell is
questions.explanation:
Height of unit cell $=\sqrt{\frac{2}{4}} 4 r$
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \text{ Base area }=6 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}(2 r)^2 \\
& \text{ Volume }=\frac{6 \sqrt{3}}{4}(2 r)^2 \cdot \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}} 4 r=24 \sqrt{2} r^3
\end{aligned}
$$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The edge length of unit cell of a metal having molecular weight $75 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}$ is 5 Å which crystallizes in cubic lattice. If the density is $2 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{cc}$ then find the radius of metal atom, $\left(N_A=6 \times 10^{23}\right)$. Give the answer in pm.
questions.solution:
For cubic lattice, $\rho=\frac{Z \times A}{N_A \times V}$ or $Z=\frac{\rho \times N_A \times V}{A}$
Given that,

$\begin{aligned}$& A=75 $\mathrm{~g}$/ $\mathrm{mol}$\\
& V=(5 Å)^3=$\left($5 $\times$10^{-8}\right)^3 $\mathrm{~cm}^$3 \\
& =125 $\times$10^{-24} $\mathrm{~cm}^$3 \\
& $N_{\mathrm{A}$}=6.02 $\times$10^{23} \\
& \rho=2 $\mathrm{gm}$/ $\mathrm{cc}$\\
& \therefore \quad Z=$\frac{2 \times 6.02 \times 10^{23} \times 125 \times 10^{-24}}{75} \approx$2 \\
&
\end{aligned}

The value of $Z$ represents that element must have body centred cubic (bcc) structure.
For bcc structure atomic radius $(r)=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 5=2.165 Å$
=216.5 $\mathrm{pm}$
